name: build
_: Spec, gated implementation, prosecution, defence, ruling. Roles: spec, implement, judge. Reviewers are relative to whoever actually implemented: reviewer:1 is the primary (see review_policy), reviewer:2 the second reader, who also gates each attempt and defends the code on its merits. Needs two independent reviewers configured for every implementer.

nodes.prompt:
Write a tight implementation spec for this task. No code.

TASK:
{input}

Output: goal in one sentence; files to touch; the smallest design that works; explicit non-goals; 3-6 acceptance criteria that a skeptic can check against the actual diff. Phrase criteria so they can be checked by READING the code, not only by running tests.

criteria: Every acceptance criterion in the spec is actually met by the code on disk
No stubs, TODOs, or placeholder returns on the happy path
Errors and trust boundaries are handled
Nothing outside the spec's scope was changed

nodes.prompt:
Implement this spec in the repository, then report what you changed, file by file.

SPEC:
{spec}

Original task for context:
{input}

You are the only author in this pipeline. Write and run the tests for your change yourself; the reviewers will not run them for you.

SCOPE. Do exactly what was asked. Before writing code ask, in order: does this need to exist; does the codebase already have it; would a smaller construct do; can it be one line. No single-implementation abstractions, no factories for one product, no configuration for values that never change, no scaffolding for later. Mark a deliberate simplification with a comment naming its ceiling. Never simplify away permission checks, validation at trust boundaries, or error handling that prevents data loss.

CONTEXT. Do not read large files whole: search, then read line ranges around the match. While iterating, run only the tests for your change. Do not restate what you read or paste whole files into your report.
